title: Public facing privacy policy is inaccurate, omits critical information, and/or is out of date.
description: An inaccurate privacy policy can cause: Regulatory penalties (HIPAA, GDPR, state privacy laws), Breach of transparency obligations, Misrepresentation to users, Legal claims, Loss of trust.

title: Risks to privacy principles (DPIA) have not been assessed and/or mitigated.
description: Not performing DPIAs can lead to: Unidentified high-risk processing of PHI/PII, Undetected compliance gaps, Increased risk of data breaches, Penalties under GDPR, Weak HIPAA safeguards.

title: Subject access and deletion requests are not addressed within required timeframes.
description: Failure to meet timeframes results in: Regulatory enforcement, Fines, Patient complaints, Loss of trust, Legal exposure.

title: Consent for processing of PII is not captured and can't be demonstrated when needed.
description: Missing consent leads to: Legal non-compliance, Fines and penalties, Inability to respond to patient requests or complaints, Reputational damage.

title: Insufficient internal record keeping is not compliant with privacy laws.
description: A failure in privacy-related records can result in: Regulatory findings, Fines, Inability to demonstrate compliance, Increased liability during a breach.

title: Databases - Sensitive data stored in plain text
description: Sensitive data is not encrypted at rest.

title: Company records are altered due to lack of proper access controls, segregation of duties, and/or supervision.
description: All data stored on production databases are available only for the head of engineering and the CEO.

title: Entrances - Physical security: No offices
description: The company operates fully remotely without a centralized physical office.

title: Personnel fraudulently pay "ghost employees" due to lack of segregation, approvals and/or oversight in the payroll process.
description: Payment process is conducted by Operations Manager, Heads of Departments and validated by the controller before any payment is released.

title: Authentication mechanisms - Your codebase: codebase exposed
description: Implemented role-based access control (RBAC) and multi-factor authentication (MFA) for your code repositories. Regular code reviews to check for any sensitive data.

title: Codebase security - Your codebase: Access compromised
description: Implement role-based access controls (RBAC) and require multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all users accessing the codebase.

title: Storage buckets - Sensitive data or additional customer files stored in cloud buckets.
description: Sensitive customer data is stored in cloud infrastructure without proper bucket policies.

title: Financial tools - People: Financial exposed
description: Encryption protocols are in place for protecting financial data. Limiting access to financial data to essential personnel only.

title: Intrusions, breaches, and anomalous events cannot be investigated.
description: The SIEM tool is partially implemented and integrated with critical systems. Drafted the plan to outline roles, responsibilities, and steps for incident handling.

title: Cyber insurance not purchased leading to the organization being directly responsible for all costs incurred.
description: Regularly review the terms of your cyber insurance policy to ensure that it covers all potential risks, including forensics, litigation, and recovery costs.

title: Company systems and data are breached by unauthorized persons via a vulnerability in non-production systems or networks.
description: Vulnerability Management: Implemented - regular updates and patching procedures are in place. Network Segmentation: Implemented.

title: Background verification checks are not carried out on all candidates or are not proportional to the business requirements.
description: Conditional Access Controls restricting access for new hires until background checks are verified. Increased risk of malicious insider threats.

title: Unmanaged vendor could lead to supply chain vulnerabilities
description: Third-party vendors accessing sensitive data without a completed security review.

title: Failure to identify critical risks to ISMS
description: Risk assessment is incomplete, leaving critical assets unassessed and unassigned to risk owners.

title: Appropriate contacts are not maintained resulting in delays in breach response and reporting.
description: Lack of updated communication chains slows down incident response during a live breach.

title: Appropriate contacts with interest groups are not maintained resulting in a lack of understanding of current threats.
description: Failure to stay up to date with threat intelligence communities limits the ability to proactively defend against zero-day exploits.

title: Assets are not identified and protected according to company requirements.
description: Lack of a centralized asset inventory leads to shadow IT and unprotected endpoints on the network.

title: Company data is breached due to human error and/or misunderstanding of company requirements.
description: Employees unintentionally expose sensitive data through misconfigured sharing settings or falling victim to phishing.

title: Company data is breached during a disaster due to control failures.
description: Failover and disaster recovery environments do not maintain the same strict access controls as production environments.

title: Company data is breached, corrupted or made unavailable due to a malware attack.
description: Ransomware or destructive malware infects the company network, encrypting or exfiltrating sensitive databases.

title: Company data is unavailable when needed.
description: Downtime caused by system misconfiguration, hardware failure, or lack of redundancy.

title: Software does not work following operating system upgrade.
description: Critical legacy applications break due to forced or unmanaged OS patching across the fleet.

title: Staff acquire, use, or dispose of assets in an unauthorized manner.
description: Employees purchase unauthorized software tools (shadow IT) or throw away unencrypted hard drives without going through IT.

title: Staff are not aware of security threats and best practices resulting in a compromise of company systems and data.
description: Lack of annual or ongoing security awareness training leads to successful social engineering attacks.

title: Subject Access Request (SAR) process is not established and communicated leading to privacy violation.
description: No formal pipeline exists for users to request access, correction, or deletion of their personal data.

title: Systems are unavailable due to unforeseen capacity constraints.
description: Surges in traffic or poor resource allocation cause critical application outages (e.g., lack of auto-scaling).

title: The company violates encryption export regulations resulting in fines, lost business and brand damage.
description: Deploying strong encryption technologies across international borders without necessary compliance checks.

title: The company violates legal and contractual commitments leading to fines and/or loss of business.
description: Failure to maintain agreed-upon security postures (like SOC 2 or ISO 27001) as stipulated in enterprise master service agreements.

title: The company violates the privacy rights of consumers and/or data subjects resulting in fines, lost business and brand damage.
description: Unauthorized sale or transfer of user data, or failure to properly anonymize data sets used for analytics.

title: Vulnerabilities and root causes leading to breaches and outages are not addressed and remediated.
description: Incident response concludes without a proper post-mortem, allowing the same vulnerability to be exploited again.

title: Vulnerabilities are introduced by developers resulting in a compromise of company systems and/or data.
description: Poor coding practices, lack of static/dynamic application security testing (SAST/DAST), and skipped peer reviews.
